sourceDecisions.note: Both Prophet honorifics and the explicit obligatory-prayer exception remain. The shared EPUB is divided at its existing Narrated Salim boundary, not treated as two independent translation sources.
The independent al-Layth/Yunus/Ibn Shihab route, Salim framing, Abdullah name, Ibn Umar attribution, night wording and Witr/obligatory-prayer clauses all remain.
The selected account says prayer without an explicit voluntary qualifier here; that qualifier is not borrowed from the English comparison. East, dismounting and qiblah remain.

Al-Sham is retained as the geographical name, rather than assigning it modern borders. The full Ibn Tahman/Hajjaj/Anas ibn Sirin/Anas/Prophet closing route and both closing honorifics remain. Historical expansions of Anas and Ibn Tahman are not imported.

The selected Arabic says Ibn Umar travelled; the historical print reads سألت ابن عمر, I asked Ibn Umar. This edition difference remains unresolved; the selected reading and its first-person did not see qualification are retained. The Quran quotation is translated only to its selected endpoint, without inserting a verse number or the remainder of the verse. The divine honorific is retained.
The complete Isa/Hafs chain, no-more-than-two clause and Abu Bakr/Umar/Uthman closing words and honorific remain separate from 1050.

The selected chain says Amr without ibn Murrah. The limited witness claim, two Prophet honorifics, eight rakahs and complete bowing/prostration remain. The first-person concluding observation is attributed to Umm Hani by quotation punctuation, without adding wording to the Arabic.

The selected full al-Layth/Yunus chain and explicit night/voluntary wording remain. The English page labels this 1054; the exact occurrence is registered without renumbering it. The EPUB appends this after Umm Hani in 2.20.207.
Head gestures and the concluding Ibn Umar practice remain. The exact first occurrence of the English page label 1055 is registered.
This is the second English page occurrence labelled 1055, not the preceding mount report. Its selected chain says Salim from his father and is not expanded with an unstated name.
The full Ibrahim ibn Tahman route remains in this separate numbered report, including both pairs of prayers. The selected expression على ظهر سير is rendered when on a journey, without adding haste.

The chain starts And from Husayn and continues the preceding route; a separate visible link supplies context without repeating invented chain words. The complete Ali ibn al-Mubarak and Harb corroboration and second Prophet honorific remain. The prayers is the understood object supplied after combined in English.

Salim’s account remains attributed. Both iqamahs, both taslims, three and two rakahs, the negative intervening-rakah and after-Isha prostration clauses and middle-of-night endpoint remain; the two negative units are not collapsed into one general sentence.
The selected chain gives Ishaq, Abd al-Samad, Harb and Yahya without expanded patronymics. The naming of the two prayers stays in the report as an explicit clarification.

The selected and modern print have ثم يجمع بينهما; the historical print has ثم يجمع بينهما ثم نزل فجمع بينهما and also the explicit before-departure clause. Those extra words are recorded here, not silently imported from that witness or from 1061. Sun declined denotes passage beyond the meridian, not sunset.
This occurrence separately retains dismounting and the explicit before-departure clause. The selected Qutaybah name is not expanded from the historical print.
The illness, sitting imam, standing followers, gesture to sit and complete selected instructions remain. No additional instructions from parallel narrations are supplied.

Both injury alternatives are retained as scratched, or grazed; al-Ayni explains the two near-synonymous verbs and narrator uncertainty. The selected Arabic and both prints have followers seated; the EPUB standing reading is not imported. The complete takbir, bowing, rising and response clauses remain; Lord, and to You preserves the selected conjunction without importing the historical Allahumma.

The two complete routes and incomplete first-route question lead-in remain in one entry. Only عن أبي بريدة is explicitly corrected to عن ابن بريدة from both prints; original input remains available. Lying down renders نائما in light of the explicit next-report Abu Abdullah gloss and Ibn Hajar’s lexical discussion; no legal qualification or sleep instruction is added. The opening if he and the two half-reward clauses remain.

The Abu Mamar alternate from Imran introduction remains in the visible narrator framing. The final Abu Abdullah lexical comment is separately attributed and fully retained; it occurs in the selected text and modern print but not the historical main text. The term nā’iman is retained in that comment so its gloss is intelligible; it is not an inserted explanation by the app.

The first-person illness and successive inability conditions remain. Abdullah is not expanded to Ibn al-Mubarak from the historical witness. Al-Mukattib retains the selected narrator epithet rather than replacing it with al-Muallim.

The Mother of the Believers designation and selected honorific position remain. Old age, night prayer and about thirty or forty verses belong to this occurrence; the third-person reporting form remains.

Both Malik routes, the mawla relationship, sitting/standing recitation, thirty-or-forty uncertainty, both rakahs and awake/asleep conclusion remain. No last-days phrase is imported from the EPUB. Freedman is the provisional relationship rendering of mawla, with independent review pending.
The narrator حبان is rendered Habban, with initial a, following the vocalized print and Ibn Hajar’s explicit name gloss. His patronymic is not inserted into the selected chain.
